did.unittitle: Report from the London Gazette on the Great Fire of London

physdescstructured.physfacet: A photo taken from a newspaper aged more than 3 centuries ago

did.abstract: A newspaper report on the first hours of the Great Fire of London and the response ordered by the king.

scopecontent.head: Transcript
scopecontent.p: About two a clock this morning a sudden and lamentable fire brake out in this City, beginning not far from Thames Street, near London Bridge; which continues still with great violence, and hath already burnt down to the ground many houses thereabouts; Which said accident affected His Majesty with that tenderness and compassion that He was pleased to Himself in Person with His Royal Highness to give order that all possible means should be used for quenching the fire, or stopping its further spreading. In which care, the Right Honourable the Earl of Craven was sent by His Majesty, to be more particularly assisting to the Lord Major and Magistrates; and several companies of His Guards sent into the City, to be helpful what ways they could in so great calamity.

did.unittitle: Wright Brothers 1908: letter to the War Office

physdescstructured.physfacet: Typed copy of a letter on one page, marked "(Copy)", headed from the Wright Brothers, 1127 W. Third Street, Dayton, Ohio, and addressed to The Secretary, War Office, London, S.W.; signed "(sd) Wright Brothers" with the initials O.W. below

did.abstract: Copy of a letter dated 10 April 1908 from the American Wright brothers in Dayton, Ohio, to the Secretary of the War Office in London. It offers to make their two-man aeroplanes for military scouting, either under a contract or by licensing the British Government to build them under their British patent, and says the United States Government had recently placed a contract with them for one machine.

descriptivenote.p: Public TNA Education page, accessed through the UK Government Web Archive, with the document image and a full transcript.

did.didnote: The TNA page describes the item as a letter from the American Wright brothers to the UK War Office about a possible contract to build their two-man aeroplanes.

scopecontent.head: Transcript
scopecontent.p: (Copy) Wright Brothers, 1127 W. Third Street, Dayton, Ohio.
The Secretary, War Office, London, S.W.

The increased interest now taken in the different countries in aeronautics, prompts to again call your attention to our aeroplane. The machines as now designed, are suitable for military scouting, being capable of carrying two men (an operator and an observer) and sufficient fuel for long flights.

We are prepared to undertake the manufacture of one or more of these machines under a contract; or, if the Government would prefer to build machines for itself under our British patent, we will grant license to operate on payment of suitable royalties on the machines so manufactured.
The United States Government has lately entered into contract with us for one of our two-men machines.

did.unittitle: Titanic Distress Telegram 1912 received by S.S. Birma

physdescstructured.physfacet: Typed on a printed Russian East Asiatic S.S. Co. form, with a table of columns for: number of words, origin station, time handed in, route and remarks; stamped M16307 and numbered 526

did.abstract: Radio-telegram sent on the night of 14/15 April 1912 at 11h45m from the Titanic (call sign MGY) and received by the S.S. Birma. It records a distress call saying the ship had struck an iceberg, was sinking fast and was asking for assistance at the position stated.

scopecontent.head: Transcript
scopecontent.p: The Russian East Asiatic S.S. Co. Radio-Telegram. S.S. "Birma".
Cgd - SOS. from M. G. Y. We have struck iceberg sinking fast come to our assistance. Position Lat. 41.46 n. Lon. 50.14. W. M. G. Y.
[MGY was the codename for the Titanic.]

did.unittitle: Birth of the NHS (1948): "Your New National Health Service" advertisement

physdescstructured.physfacet: Printed single-page public information advertisement, digitised as an image

did.abstract: A public information advertisement issued by the Department of Health for Scotland to explain that the National Health Service would start on 5 July 1948. It says that anyone can use the service, with no age limits and no fees, and tells people to choose a doctor and to collect application form E.C.1 for each family member. It appeared in selected Sunday, morning and evening newspapers in Scotland.

dao.linktitle: Birth of the NHS 1948 - The National Archives

scopecontent.p: Advertisement that introduces the new National Health Service to the public in Scotland shortly before it began. It explains who can use the service, how it is paid for through public funds and how people should register with a doctor.

did.abstract: Telegram from the Foreign and Commonwealth Office to Washington, 21 July 1969, conveying Prime Minister Harold Wilson’s congratulations to President Nixon and the Apollo 11 astronauts on the successful Moon landing.

scopecontent.p: Educational resource based on a restricted telegram about the Apollo 11 mission.
